[strategy/guidance/security/Identity/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-IAM-ZTA-AUTH-RAD-2.3.02.md#purpose-and-scope]

## Purpose and Scope

This RAD provides illustrative patterns for the authentication and federation capability cluster — showing how the Identity Broker, SSO, and MFA Component ABBs compose to deliver Zero Trust continuous verification.

**Paired ABBs**:
- [GUID-SEC-IAM-IDENTITY-BROKER-2.2.02](../GUID-SEC-IAM-IDENTITY-BROKER-2.2.02.md) — Identity Broker and Federation
- [GUID-SEC-IAM-SSO-2.2.03](../GUID-SEC-IAM-SSO-2.2.03.md) — Single Sign-On
- [GUID-SEC-IAM-MFA-2.2.04](../GUID-SEC-IAM-MFA-2.2.04.md) — Multifactor Authentication

**In Scope**: Federation topology, session lifecycle, step-up authentication, phishing-resistant authenticator integration, cross-domain federation, session revocation

**Out of Scope**: Identity proofing (see GUID-SEC-IAM-PROOFING-RAD-2.3.04), PAM workflows (see GUID-SEC-IAM-PAM-RAD-2.3.03)

[strategy/guidance/security/Identity/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-IAM-ZTA-AUTH-RAD-2.3.02.md#capability-domain-boundary]

### Capability Domain Boundary

This cluster's scope begins at the user's initial authentication request and ends at the enterprise session token issued to the consuming application. The application is responsible for validating the token and enforcing application-level authorization; this RAD does not govern post-issuance authorization.

[strategy/guidance/security/Identity/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-IAM-ZTA-AUTH-RAD-2.3.02.md#flow-1-internal-workforce-identity--sso-with-risk-adaptive-step-up]

#### Flow 1: Internal Workforce Identity — SSO with Risk-Adaptive Step-Up

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor User as Workforce User
    participant App as Application
    participant IdP as Enterprise IdP
    participant MFA as MFA Service

    User->>App: Request access
    App-->>IdP: Redirect — authentication request (OIDC/SAML)
    Note over IdP: Evaluate session, AAL, risk context
    alt No valid session or step-up required
        IdP->>MFA: Challenge user (AAL-required factor)
        MFA-->>IdP: Authenticator verified (AAL met)
    end
    Note over IdP: Issue session token scoped to application
    IdP-->>App: Redirect with access token / assertion
    App-->>User: Access granted
```
page_texts.10:
[strategy/guidance/security/Identity/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-IAM-ZTA-AUTH-RAD-2.3.02.md#flow-2-external--partner-user-identity--cross-domain-federation-with-enterprise-step-up]

#### Flow 2: External / Partner User Identity — Cross-Domain Federation with Enterprise Step-Up

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor ExtUser as "External / Partner User"
    participant App as Application
    participant Broker as Identity Broker
    participant ExtIdP as "External IdP (Home)"
    participant IdP as Enterprise IdP
    participant MFA as MFA Service

    ExtUser->>App: Request access
    App-->>Broker: Redirect — authentication request (OIDC/SAML)
    Note over Broker: Select home IdP and initiate outbound federation
    Broker-->>ExtUser: Redirect to External IdP
    ExtUser->>ExtIdP: Authenticate at home IdP
    ExtIdP-->>Broker: Return signed assertion (ACS)
    Note over Broker: Validate signature, audience, and federation agreement then normalize attributes
    Broker-->>IdP: Forward normalized identity assertion
    Note over IdP: Evaluate assertion AAL against enterprise policy and apply risk context
    alt Enterprise step-up required
        IdP->>MFA: Challenge for enterprise-controlled factor
        MFA-->>IdP: Authenticator verified (AAL met)
    end
    IdP-->>App: Enterprise session token (scoped to partner entitlements)
    App-->>ExtUser: Access granted
```

[strategy/guidance/security/Identity/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-IAM-ZTA-AUTH-RAD-2.3.02.md#pattern-1-risk-adaptive-step-up-authentication]

### Pattern 1: Risk-Adaptive Step-Up Authentication

**When to use**: User holds an active SSO session at AAL1 and requests access to a resource requiring AAL2 or above

**Logical flow**:
1. Application signals its AAL requirement in the authentication request
2. IdP evaluates current session AAL against the requirement
3. If the session AAL is insufficient, IdP invokes the MFA service for a step-up challenge at the required level
4. On successful challenge, session AAL is elevated for the duration of the access
5. Session AAL reverts to baseline at configurable timeout or logout

**Illustrative technology class**: Identity provider with continuous access evaluation (CAE) and risk-signal integration

---
page_texts.14:
[strategy/guidance/security/Identity/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-IAM-ZTA-AUTH-RAD-2.3.02.md#pattern-2-external-partner-cross-domain-federation]

### Pattern 2: External Partner Cross-Domain Federation

**When to use**: Government agency partners, subcontractors, or healthcare organizations with their own IdP that require access to enterprise services

**Logical flow**:
1. Partner user authenticates against their home IdP (SAML 2.0 or OIDC)
2. Home IdP issues an assertion to the enterprise Identity Broker
3. Broker validates signature, audience, and federation agreement; normalizes attribute claims
4. Broker forwards a translated, attribute-normalized assertion to the enterprise IdP
5. Enterprise IdP applies local authorization policy, issues a session scoped to the partner's entitlements

**Illustrative technology class**: Identity broker with bilateral SAML 2.0 / OIDC federation and attribute mapping engine

---
page_texts.15:
[strategy/guidance/security/Identity/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-IAM-ZTA-AUTH-RAD-2.3.02.md#pattern-3-single-logout-propagation]

### Pattern 3: Single Logout Propagation

**When to use**: User-initiated logout, security-initiated session revocation, or administrative session termination

**Logical flow**:
1. Logout event is triggered (user-initiated, timeout, or administrative revocation)
2. IdP invalidates the enterprise session
3. IdP propagates logout signal to all applications with active sessions via SLO endpoint (SAML Single Logout or OIDC back-channel logout)
4. Applications receiving the SLO signal invalidate their local session state
5. Audit event recorded for logout completeness and timing

[strategy/guidance/security/Identity/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-IAM-ZTA-AUTH-RAD-2.3.02.md#deployment-context-considerations]

## Deployment Context Considerations

| Context | Architectural Consideration |
|---|---|
| Cloud-hosted applications | Applications SHOULD use OIDC for session integration; SAML 2.0 is supported for legacy applications that cannot adopt OIDC |
| On-premises applications | Legacy authentication protocols (Kerberos, LDAP bind) must be mediated through the identity broker; direct application-to-directory authentication is prohibited for new integrations |
| Mobile and native applications | PKCE-protected OIDC authorization code flow SHALL be used; implicit flow is prohibited |
| Phishing-resistant authenticators | Passkeys (FIDO2/WebAuthn) and hardware security keys are the illustrative technology class for AAL3-equivalent patterns; SMS-based OTP is not considered phishing-resistant |

---

[strategy/guidance/security/Identity/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-IAM-ZTA-AUTH-RAD-2.3.02.md#constraints-and-exceptions]

## Constraints and Exceptions

- Session AAL elevation does not retroactively upgrade the trust level of prior actions taken in the lower-AAL session
- Federation trust agreements with external partners require governance approval before technical configuration; technical federation configuration without a current agreement is prohibited
- Applications that cannot support single logout must document this gap and implement compensating controls (short session lifetimes, forced re-authentication)
